SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JUNE 12, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Sierra Room.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk Division Manager.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  OEC Group (Business Spotlight). A proclamation was also presented from Assemblymember
  Sharon Quirk-Silva by Joe Pak, Field Representative.

  Bob and Mary Buell (75th Wedding Anniversary). Proclamations were also presented from
  Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva and U.S. Senator Alex Padilla by Joe Pak, Field
  Representative for Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva.

  In honor of Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month:

  Buddhist Tzu Chi Foundation, Cerritos Chinese American Senior Citizen Association,
  Cerritos Folk Dancers, Cerritos Indo American Seniors, Cerritos Ivy Club, Cerritos
  Korean Soccer Club, Cerritos Shalom Tigers Soccer Club, Chinese Culture
  Association of Southern California, Da Hawaii Seniors Club, Filipino Seniors of
  Cerritos Association, Formosa Senior Association, Global Culture Education
  Foundation, Green Angels Mission Soccer, JC Culture Foundation, Korean American
  OB Soccer Club, Mid-City Korean American Senior Association, Rayshine
  Foundation, SAAHAS for Cause, and The Original Happy Seniors of Cerritos

  Proclamations were also presented from Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva by Joe Pak, Field
  Representative. Additionally, the Mayor presented proclamations from Congresswoman Michelle
  Steel.

Pursuant to City Council consensus, Item 9A was heard at this juncture of the meeting. The detail
for Item 9A is listed in the appropriate section below.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Gail Grossman commented on her years of service to the community, including her
  appointments to various City Commissions and Committees, and announced her
  resignation from the Community Safety Committee.

  The members of the City Council expressed their gratitude to Gail Grossman for her years
  of service to the community and as an appointed City Commission/Committee member.

  Teddy Lloyd inquired whether tennis courts could be utilized for pickleball practice at
  Liberty Park.

  Al Barlevy commented on Councilmember Johnson’s 2022 request to remove one of her
  appointees and expressed concern regarding certain Councilmembers’ votes in opposition.

  Ram Kakkar requested the City address his concerns regarding the Cerritos Sports Complex
  (restrooms, external lighting on southside of walking path). He also requested
  improvements to the sound systems for the hearing impaired at the Cerritos Senior Center.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted written
  correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Matthew Ellis submitted comments regarding the condition of the water fountains at the
  Cerritos Towne Center.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.
